id_and_class.summary: Amanda Gefter proposes uniting QBism, which treats quantum theory as a user’s manual for agents in a participatory universe, with enactivism, which treats cognition as an organism enacting the boundary between itself and its world. QBism explains how the world is made and remade through an agent’s interactions; enactivism explains how agents are made and remade through interactions with the world. Together, Gefter argues, they give one post-Cartesian metaphysics in which self and world are co-enacted.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Self and World Co-Enacted Through Participation

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness belongs to the ongoing, normatively constrained enactment of the subject–object boundary, in which agent and world bring each other forth through interaction.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Gefter rejects an absolute subject–object split, the precondition for both materialism and idealism. The body is ‘an ongoing verb rather than a pregiven noun’, making itself in participation with the world and functioning as both subject and object.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (the view rejects the split that would make either subject or object the foundation from which the other emerges)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Selves emerge in participatory ‘between spaces’, neither in private first-person interiors nor in detached third-person views; Gefter calls this second-person primacy. Experiences are not private and beliefs are not internal representations.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Agents and worlds as co-enacted processes, quantum measurement as an act that enacts the subject–object divide, autopoietic living systems, and shared social processes with their own norms.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through embodied, skilled engagement and live social interaction rather than detached observation; knowledge is knowing-how, not propositional content.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: From enactivism: autopoiesis (self-production and self-distinction), sense-making (normative engagement that matters for viability), knowledge-how, and second-person primacy. From QBism: agents whose measurements enact the subject–object divide.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Experience, Agency, Self and world, Intersubjectivity, Normativity
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Mutual enactment: quantum measurement enacts the subject–object divide from the world’s side, and cognition enacts it from the agent’s side, as two halves of one participatory process.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Self and world are continually created and recreated; novelty arises in the dynamic, precarious, participatory ‘between’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In the relation between agent and world, and between agents, not inside a head or in an external world taken alone.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Sense-making guides an organism’s actions according to what matters for its continued viability; in social coordination, shared processes generate new meaning.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Both QBism and enactivism are anti-representational: there are no static internal models corresponding to an external reality.
core_claims_and_evidence: QBism needs enactivism’s non-Cartesian definitions of agent, experience, belief and normativity to answer charges of solipsism and idealism.
Enactivism needs QBism’s participatory physics, since acting within a classical, observer-independent world would make it incoherent.
Intersubjective agreement is achieved in live interaction, as in De Jaegher and Di Paolo’s participatory sense-making, rather than fixed by pre-existing facts.
Both frameworks oppose the same 17th-century Cartesian split, so each tells half of one story.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical synthesis of quantum foundations (QBism) and enactive cognitive science

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Classification is contested: Gefter denies her view is materialist, while Kuhn places enactivism under Materialism because it posits nothing beyond current physics but would not classify QBism there. Both QBism and enactivism already face uphill battles against entrenched views of world and self.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Gefter offers the synthesis as a possibility; how co-enactment of self and world accounts for the felt quality of experience is not worked out.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally consistent in rejecting the subject–object split on both the physics and cognition sides. It sits outside the standard materialism–idealism–dualism map, which is the point of the view.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since agents arise through autopoiesis and sense-making, a system that does not produce and maintain itself in engagement with its world would not count as an agent in the enactive sense.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: The self exists only as an ongoing enactment by a living body in participation with its world, which gives nothing to continue once that process stops.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Gefter envisions a participatory ontology where meaning, agency and reality are inseparable from the acts that bring them forth, so meaning is part of how reality itself is constituted.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Anti-representationalism means there is no internal model of a self to copy; the self is a living process of engagement.
